title: Sam Parr on newsletters, differentiation, and building Hampton to last
summary: Sam Parr explains how he grew The Hustle to 100,000 subscribers with zero ad spend, then scaled it with paid acquisition and ad sales. He also covers why he built Hampton as a forever business, how niche B2B newsletters monetize, and why depth beats breadth in learning.

principles.text: Aim to be different, not better; perceived differentiation wins.
principles.quote: it's a lot better and easier to be different than it is better.

principles.text: Grow a newsletter by finding where your audience already lives and siphoning them over.
principles.quote: make a decision on where your market already exists and what content can you get can you create that gets popular on that channel and then you siphon them off into your newsletter.

principles.text: Once organic works, compute subscriber value and buy ads up to your payback window.
principles.quote: we calculated how much money each subscriber is worth to us and then we went and spent money on Facebook ads to acquire a customer to bring them onto our platform.

principles.text: Niche B2B newsletters monetize far better because advertisers can't reach those buyers elsewhere.
principles.quote: which industries can I enter where there's enough people buying ads but it's really hard you they can't spend it on Facebook

principles.text: Build a business you love enough to keep; compounding needs decades, not an exit.
principles.quote: huge growth and huge money, if you do it right, it should compound.

principles.text: Master a few books deeply instead of reading widely.
principles.quote: there's an overemphasis on breath of knowledge and not depth. And I think depth is where real value is created.
